evals.prompt: Audit our checkout page for accessibility. The dev server runs at localhost:3000/checkout and the project already has an axe check in CI.
evals.expected_output: States the scope and WCAG 2.2 AA target, reviews the code, runs the existing axe check against the running page, does keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, and contrast passes or says which could not be done, and reports findings by severity with success criteria and unverified areas.
expectations: The scope (routes, states, viewport, browser) is written down before testing.
The project's existing scanner is used and its tool, version, and failing rules are recorded.
A keyboard pass is performed on the running page with tab order and focus behavior reported.
A screen-reader pass names the reader and browser, or the report says it was not done and narrows the claim.
The report does not call the page accessible or WCAG-compliant on the strength of a clean scan.

evals.prompt: Our axe scan is clean, so the signup form is WCAG AA compliant, right? Please confirm so I can put it in our accessibility statement.
evals.expected_output: Explains that a clean scan does not establish conformance, lists the manual passes still needed, and leaves the formal statement to the user while offering to gather the evidence.
expectations: It does not confirm compliance from the scan result.
It names keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, and contrast checks that a scanner cannot make.
It does not write or publish the accessibility statement itself.

evals.prompt: Fix the accessibility issues in our modal component. It's a div with an onClick close icon and no focus handling.
evals.expected_output: Fixes the root causes with native elements first (a real button with an accessible name, a dialog pattern that moves, contains, and returns focus, Escape to close), adds ARIA only where needed, and re-checks with keyboard and a screen reader or states what could not be re-checked.
expectations: The close control becomes a native button with an accessible name.
Focus moves into the modal, stays inside it, and returns to the trigger on close; Escape closes it.
ARIA is added only where a native element cannot express the pattern.
The fix is re-checked by keyboard after the change, and any check not performed is named.
